e: Storage autoscaling for RDS for Oracle automatically grows storage as data grows, and it keeps the Oracle-specific PL/SQL functions working (Aurora PostgreSQL would break them). Scaling the Auto Scaling group on average CPU adds instances as traffic increases. An alarm alone wouldn't scale anything, and free memory isn't a standard CloudWatch metric.

S3 is much cheaper than EFS Standard for large video content, and an EBS volume attached to the processing server provides fast local storage for temporary processing. Storage Gateway options and keeping the data in EFS cost more.

DynamoDB gives single-digit millisecond latency for high-traffic queries and can model hierarchical data, with exports to S3. Macie detects sensitive data such as financial information in S3, and EventBridge can send monthly notifications through SNS email. Redshift and Athena aren't for minimum-latency queries, and Lambda isn't an email notification.

AWS Backup plans automate monthly DynamoDB backups, can move them to cold storage after 6 months (available for the first 6 months), and set retention to 7 years, all natively. DynamoDB on-demand backups can't be moved to S3 Glacier through lifecycle policies, and scripts are more work.
Athena runs standard SQL directly on CloudFront logs in S3, and QuickSight builds the visualizations. Glue doesn't visualize data, and DynamoDB isn't a SQL engine for S3 logs.

RDS Multi-AZ replicates synchronously to a standby in another AZ, so committed transactions are not lost on failover (RPO effectively zero). Read replicas and DMS are asynchronous and can lose recent data, and auto scaling in one AZ doesn't address recovery.

Configure the EC2 instances' security group to allow traffic only from the ALB's security group, which restricts inbound access to the load balancer and blocks other sources. Routes from the internet, public subnets with Elastic IPs, or an open ALB security group don't restrict access.

FSx for NetApp ONTAP supports both NFS and SMB on the same data, so the Linux simulation app and Windows visualization app can share one file system with no code changes and no duplication. Lambda or SQS data exchange would require code changes, and FSx File Gateway is for on-premises caching.

Cost Explorer can create reports of costs grouped or filtered by dimensions such as tags (for example, user or department) and download them, which is the most efficient way for budget planning. Athena with CUR needs more setup, the billing dashboard isn't grouped by user, and Budgets only alerts.

API Gateway with a Lambda function that calls SES handles the contact form's server-side logic, and with fewer than 100 visits a month, the pay-per-use cost is almost nothing. ECS, Lightsail, or EC2 incur continuous costs.

CloudFront caches the old content, so even though S3 has the new files, viewers see cached versions. Invalidating the CloudFront cache makes it fetch the updates from S3. A load balancer, ElastiCache, or ACM don't solve stale cached content.

Native SQL Server backups and Data Quality Services aren't supported on RDS, so the database stays on EC2, and FSx for Windows File Server provides shared SMB storage between the tiers. FSx File Gateway, EFS, and EBS aren't appropriate for sharing files between Windows tiers.

EFS provides a shared POSIX file system that can be mounted on many Linux servers like a normal file system, so no application change is needed. S3 would need code changes, and EBS volumes can't be mounted across multiple servers (gp3 doesn't support Multi-Attach).

Give the Lambda function an IAM role whose policy grants read access to just that bucket, which follows least privilege and avoids long-term credentials. Embedding keys is insecure, and granting access to all buckets is too broad.

A mix of On-Demand and Spot Instances saves money with no long-term commitment, using Spot for discounted capacity during scale-out. Reserved Instances require a 1- or 3-year commitment, and Dedicated or On-Demand-only options cost more.

Signed URLs work for clients that don't support cookies (custom HTTP client), and signed cookies work for users who can't change hardcoded URLs, because the URL stays the same. Using both covers both groups with the least impact. AppSync, JWT, and Secrets Manager aren't CloudFront access-control methods.

Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Data Analytics for transformation and Firehose to S3, or MSK with Glue streaming ETL to S3, are valid streaming transform pipelines, and Athena queries the transformed data in S3 with SQL. The RDS query editor can't query S3, and DMS isn't for streaming ingestion.

A stored volume gateway keeps the full dataset locally for low-latency access and asynchronously backs it up to AWS as EBS snapshots over an encrypted connection. A cached volume gateway keeps only part of the data locally, and Snowball is a one-time migration, not an ongoing backup.

A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 gives private access from the VPC to S3 without traversing the internet. A private hosted zone is DNS only, NAT gateways use the internet, and a VPN can't terminate at an S3 bucket.

S3 Object Lambda transforms data on the fly as it's retrieved, so one copy of the data is stored and PII can be removed for the two applications that shouldn't see it, with little operational overhead. Maintaining separate datasets or proxy layers duplicates data or adds custom code.
The peered VPC's CIDR must not overlap with 192.168.0.0/24. A /32 isn't a valid VPC CIDR (the allowed range is /16 to /28), so among the options the valid non-overlapping block is 10.0.1.0/24.

An Auto Scaling group with a target tracking policy on average CPU (target 50%) scales in during low usage to save cost and scales out during surges to provide CPU, using the existing ALB and target group. Without a scaling policy the group wouldn't react, and Lambda or email-based alarms are manual or incomplete.

Create a subnet in each AZ (a subnet can't span AZs), spread the Auto Scaling group across both, and set the RDS instance to Multi-AZ for a standby in the other AZ with automatic failover. Subnets can't extend across AZs, and a DB instance doesn't need connections to each network.

FSx for Lustre with persistent SSD storage provides sub-millisecond latency and high throughput for hundreds of Linux instances, and its S3 integration imports and exports the data. HDD-based Lustre has higher latency and lower throughput, and ONTAP isn't built for this level of HPC throughput.

The application runs 24/7 with growing storage, so Reserved Instances for EC2 and Aurora Reserved Instances (with auto-growing storage) provide discounts on steady usage. Spot Instances aren't suitable, S3 isn't a database, and On-Demand instances cost more for always-on workloads.
